skill.name: research-lookup
skill.description: Look up current research information using Perplexity's Sonar Pro Search or Sonar Reasoning Pro models through OpenRouter. Automatically selects the best model based on query complexity. Search academic papers, recent studies, technical documentation, and general research information with citations.
skill.summary: Search current scholarly sources through OpenRouter with automatic model selection and citation extraction.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The skill reads one documented API key and performs expected HTTPS requests to OpenRouter. Most high-severity detections are key names, placeholders, or text references, not hardcoded secrets or environment-file reads. Queries leave the local system, and SKILL.md recommends one nonbundled generator command that requires explicit dependency review.

remediation.issue: Research queries leave the local environment
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before transmitting queries and state that confidential, personal, or unpublished material should not be submitted.

remediation.issue: The schematic generator command targets an absent script
remediation.suggestion: Bundle the referenced generator, remove the command, or require confirmation after resolving the script to a trusted installed dependency.
Keep one ResearchLookup implementation so endpoint, model, and credential behavior cannot diverge between duplicate files.

content.user_title: Research Current Literature with Cited Sources
content.value_statement: Finding current scholarly evidence and reliable citations takes time. This skill queries Perplexity Sonar through OpenRouter and organizes results with source links.
actual_capabilities: Sends single or batch research queries to Perplexity Sonar models through OpenRouter.
Selects a search or reasoning model using keywords, query length, and question count.
Requests academic search mode with a high search context.
Extracts source metadata, DOI links, and selected scholarly URLs from returned responses.
Supports manual model selection and command-line output with timestamps and token usage.
limitations: Requires an OpenRouter API key, account credits, and network access.
Sends complete research queries to OpenRouter and Perplexity, so confidential material should be removed.
Generated summaries and citations can be inaccurate, so every claim and primary source requires verification.
The included examples.py complexity demo calls a method absent from ResearchLookup and may fail.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Literature Review
use_cases.description: Find recent studies, key findings, and source links before drafting a literature review.

use_cases.title: Verify Technical Claims
use_cases.description: Check claims and gather citation details for manuscripts, reports, or technical documentation.

use_cases.title: Compare Research Evidence
use_cases.description: Compare evidence, methods, limitations, and unresolved questions across several studies.

prompt_templates.title: Find Recent Studies
prompt_templates.prompt: Find peer-reviewed studies about [topic] published since [year]. Summarize the main findings and list source links with DOI details.
prompt_templates.scenario: A first literature search on a focused topic.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a Research Claim
prompt_templates.prompt: Check this claim against recent scholarly evidence: [claim]. State whether evidence supports it and identify conflicting findings.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Methods or Findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [approach A] and [approach B] for [use case]. Evaluate effectiveness, limitations, study quality, and important trade-offs with citations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Choosing between technical or scientific approaches.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Critical Evidence Synthesis
prompt_templates.prompt: Synthesize research on [question] using studies from [date range]. Separate consensus, conflicting evidence, methodological weaknesses, and research gaps. Include verification links.

output_examples.input: Find recent peer-reviewed studies on off-target effects in CRISPR gene editing.
output: A concise summary of recurring findings and reported mitigation strategies.
Key studies grouped by method, publication date, and evidence strength.
Source links, DOI details, limitations, and open research questions.

output_examples.input: Compare transformer models and recurrent neural networks for clinical time-series analysis.
output: A structured comparison of accuracy, data needs, interpretability, and computational cost.
Areas of agreement and conflict across recent studies.
Cited sources with verification links and cautions about study quality.

best_practices: Use precise topics, date ranges, populations, and requested evidence types.
Remove confidential, personal, or unpublished information before submitting a query.
Open each cited source and verify its metadata, methods, and claimed findings.
anti_patterns: Do not treat generated citations or summaries as verified evidence.
Do not submit broad questions without a field, time frame, or research objective.
Do not use the output alone for medical, legal, safety, or policy decisions.

faq.question: Does this skill require an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. You need an OpenRouter account, an OPENROUTER_API_KEY environment variable, credits, and network access.

faq.question: Where are my research queries sent?
faq.answer: The skill sends each query and the API key to OpenRouter, which routes the request to a Perplexity Sonar model.

faq.question: Are returned citations already verified?
faq.answer: No. Open every cited source and confirm authors, title, date, DOI, and claimed findings before use.

faq.question: How does automatic model selection work?
faq.answer: Queries with analytical keywords, multiple questions, or greater length use the reasoning model. Simpler queries use the search model.

faq.question: Can the skill process several queries?
faq.answer: Yes. The command-line tool accepts multiple queries and inserts a configurable delay between requests.

faq.question: Can it access paywalled papers?
faq.answer: The service may return metadata or summaries, but it cannot guarantee full-text access to paywalled or restricted sources.
